injuries.detail: Wilson didn't practice Wednesday, but he was out there Thursday in a limited capacity. He'll likely need another limited session Friday to avoid an injury designation ahead of the Week 8 meeting with the Cowboys.

Beck has been battling a back injury, though it hasn't prevented him from being the team's emergency QB3. While it appears the worst of the injury is behind the rookie signal-caller, that still likely won't improve his chances of getting on the field anytime soon, at least while Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew are healthy.

For a second day in a row, Wilson was donning a yellow non-contact jersey on the practice field, and he received the same limited listing as a result. He relayed to Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com on Wednesday that he's tending to sore ribs, but there's been no indication that he's in danger of missing Sunday's game in Dallas. Friday's injury report will reveal if Wilson has a designation ahead of that matchup.

After Allgeier sat out Wednesday's session due to a toe injury, his ability to mix into drills one day later generally is a good sign as the Cardinals go through Week 8 prep. Friday's practice report will unveil if Allgeier enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, and also whether or not rookie RB Jeremiyah Love has a chance to put an end to a two-game absence. Currently, Bam Knight is the only healthy backfield option on Arizona's active roster.

Love maintained his activity level from Wednesday, which followed two weeks off due to a lingering ankle injury. Head coach Mike LaFleur hasn't indicated if Love actually has a chance to return to action Sunday at Dallas, but Friday's practice report will reveal his chances to do so.
questionable

Wingard has been sidelined for the Cardinals' past three games due to a bone bruise in his knee he sustained back in Week 4 against the Giants, and now his availability for Week 8 is in question. If he can upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, there's a good chance he'll suit up Sunday at Dallas.
questionable

Baker was cleared to play against the Broncos after nursing a groin injury and an illness during Week 7 prep. He was on the field for 59 of the Cardinals' 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent), but his two stops were a season low. The veteran safety is up to 44 tackles (25 solo), including a career-best 3.5 sacks, and four pass defenses (including one interception) through seven regular-season games.

Gibbens' 41 defensive snaps were a season low, but the fifth-year linebacker still led the Cardinals in tackles. He's posted at least seven stops in six of seven regular-season games and is up to 49 tackles (21 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass defense in 2026.

injuries.evidence: The transaction comes after Brooks announced earlier in the day that he underwent season-ending wrist surgery.
injuries.detail: The transaction comes after Brooks announced earlier in the day that he underwent season-ending wrist surgery. Brooks saw light snaps through the first four weeks of the season, but he stepped in as the Cardinals' No. 3 wideout for the past three games after Marvin Harrison was traded to the Texans. The 26-year-old will finish the 2026 campaign with five receptions for 81 yards on 17 targets to go with 499 yards on 19 kickoff returns.

Higgins played 39 offensive snaps and 17 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The versatile tight end continues to fill a moderate role in the passing game, allowing the Cardinals to continue playing 12- and 13-personnel packages.

Coming off the heels of a second straight five-catch game, Bourne had positive momentum heading into Week 7. However, while his six targets were encouraging, his production was less efficient than a team baseline that was already not very good. With that said, teammate Jalen Brooks suffered a season-ending wrist injury Sunday, leaving Bourne as the Cardinals' undisputed second option at wide receiver moving forward.

Reiman hasn't played this season and is currently on the reserve/PUP list. While there haven't been any updates on when the 25-year-old will be back on the field, it appears the door isn't fully closed regarding his return before the end of the 2026 campaign. Reiman has appeared in 21 regular-season games for the Cardinals since being drafted in the third round in the 2024 NFL Draft, amassing nine catches for 55 yards.

It's a typical LaFleur non-answer type of answer. It was reported two weeks ago that Conner was close to practicing, but there's been no indication his 21-day practice window is close to being opened by the Cardinals. There's not much room on the depth chart for another running back that doesn't play special teams in Arizona.

With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined for a second consecutive contest, Tyler Allgeier and Knight again were tasked with manning the Cardinals backfield. Allgeier earned 11 touches to Knight's 10 on Sunday, but the latter out-gained him by 14 yards from scrimmage (63 versus 49). It was the second week in a row in which Knight churned out more yardage than Allgeier on fewer touches, and even if Love is able to return in Week 8 at Dallas, Knight could begin to put himself in position for regular snaps moving forward, if he hasn't already.

After failing to score a touchdown in the Week 6 win over the Rams, Brissett and the Cardinals mustered only one touchdown on five trips into the red zone Sunday. Brissett averaged a meager 5.7 yards per pass attempt but inflated his numbers with heavy volume. He has a 3-16 record since taking over as Arizona's starting QB while throwing at least 40 passes in 10 of those 19 starts. Brissett is likely to post a more efficient passing performance in Week 8 against a far more permissive Cowboys pass defense.

Ryland remained a busy man in Week 7, making field goals from 30, 26 and 41 yards against the Broncos. The kicker has now registered three or more field-goal makes in four contests this season while attempting one or zero field goals in Arizona's other three games. Ryland and the Cardinals' unpredictable offense will have a chance to be more productive in Week 8 against the Cowboys' putrid defense.

McBride became the first tight end in NFL history to record 400 regular-season catches in his first five campaigns, bolstering his career total to 406 with 10 grabs Sunday. He scored Arizona's lone touchdown of the game on a seven-yard catch in the third quarter while setting season highs in catches and receiving yards. McBride has recorded at least seven receptions in all seven games this season while scoring four times heading into a Week 8 matchup with a weak Dallas pass defense.

Terrell recently returned for Sunday's win over the 49ers after missing four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury. He practiced in full Wednesday, and while he was limited Thursday, the Falcons may just be playing it safe ahead of the Week 8 meeting with the Buccaneers. For now, Terrell should at least be considered questionable for that contest, though more clarity on his status will likely be revealed Friday.

Henderson practiced in full Wednesday. He was downgraded to limited Thursday, popping up on the practice report due to a groin injury that he's dealt with in the last few weeks. With A.J. Terrell (groin) and Avieon Terrell (illness) also in danger of missing the Week 8 meeting with Tampa, Mike Hughes, Mike Ford and Robert Longerbeam may see more action.

Daniels practiced in full Wednesday, though after being downgraded to limited Thursday, there is concern he won't be on the field in Week 8 versus Tampa Bay. The 23-year-old is coming off the best performance of his career in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, garnering 11 tackles (nine solo) and one interception. His services will be needed even more if Divine Deablo (forearm) can't suit up once again. However, if Deablo and Daniels are both sidelined, Harold Perkins, Christian Harris and Josh Woods would likely be more involved.

Deablo injured his forearm during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, which ultimately kept him off the field for Sunday's win over the 49ers. The 28-year-old didn't practice Wednesday, and while he was limited Thursday, he likely has more hurdles to clear before suiting up Sunday versus Tampa Bay. If Deablo can't get out there in Week 8, Harold Perkins and Kendal Daniels (Achilles) could be in line for more snaps.

Zaccheaus didn't play in the 29-20 win over San Francisco on Sunday. While his limited participation in the Falcons' previous two practices is a positive sign, he still may be heading for an injury designation for the Week 8 meeting with Tampa Bay. The 29-year-old hasn't been overly involved this season, catching four passes (11 targets) for 17 yards. However, Zaccheaus plays a role as a return man on special teams, so if he's not cleared to play Sunday, Jahan Dotson and Zachariah Branch may see more action in that area, even more so if Brian Robinson (hamstring) is also unavailable.
questionable

Robinson has yet to resume practicing after sitting out Atlanta's Week 7 win over the 49ers due to a hamstring injury. Robinson will likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to avoid being ruled out for a second consecutive game, in which case Khalil Herbert would likely be elevated from the practice squad to work as Bijan Robinson's backup again.

Watts missed just three defensive snaps, as he continues to be a key part of Atlanta's secondary. The second-year safety has posted seven or more tackles in four of his seven games so far this season and leads the Falcons with 44 tackles (including 0.5 sacks). He also has two defensed passes, including an interception.

Bates contributed in multiple ways during a big day for Atlanta's defense. He finished tied for second on the team with nine stops and picked off Brock Purdy midway through the third quarter as San Francisco was approaching the red zone. For good measure, Bates sealed the win by forcing a George Kittle fumble with less than a minute remaining in the contest. Bates' nine stops were a season high, and the interception was his first of the campaign.

Perkins' tackle total was tied for second on Atlanta behind fellow rookie Kendal Daniels. Perkins finished with his second-highest number of stops so far, trailing only the 10 tackles he recorded Week 4 in New Orleans. Perkins made his first NFL start Sunday, as Divine Deablo was sidelined due to a forearm injury.

questionable

Branch saw minimal usage offensively, but he made an impact early with a 61-yard kickoff return in the first quarter, with the Falcons' offense converting that opportunity into a 39-yard field goal five plays later. It was a solid bounce back from his Week 6 performance against the Chicago, when he lost two fumbles. The rookie third-rounder has a 10-64-0 line on 12 targets through seven regular-season games, and Branch's role will continue to be a complementary one while he's situated behind Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson in the pecking order. The Falcons will hit the road for Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 1.

Hooper played 29 offensive snaps and four special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The No. 3 tight end was utilized as a blocker and pass catcher but was outshined by No. 4 option Nick Muse, who caught a key touchdown as the team took down the undefeated 49ers.

Dotson's lone catch came late in the second quarter as part of a 14-play, 56-yard drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal by Nick Folk as time expired. Dotson also drew a defensive pass interference penalty late in the third quarter, but it was an otherwise quiet night for the fifth-year pro, whose 38 offensive snaps were second-most among Falcons wide receivers behind Drake London (55). Dotson has two catches or fewer in six of the first seven games of the regular season for a 12-242-2 line on 26 targets. The Falcons hit the road in Week 8 for an NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers, whose defense stifled Panthers QB Bryce Young in a Week 7 win for Tampa Bay.

Muse played 21 offensive snaps and 20 special-teams snaps in Sunday's game. The No. 4 tight end proved that versatility can lead to production, making the most of his red-zone opportunities and recording a key score as the Falcons handed the 49ers their first loss of the season.

Herbert was elevated to the active roster for Sunday's 29-20 win against the 49ers, when he served as Bijan Robinson's backup due to the absence of Brian Robinson (hamstring). Herbert was on the field for only 11 of the Falcons' 68 snaps (16.2 percent), although he nearly nearly found the end zone early in the second half on a 19-yard catch but was ruled out of bounds just short of the goal line. The sixth-year running back added two carries for nine yards and turned two kickoff returns into 65 yards, and he could be elevated for Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 1 depending on the health of the Falcons' backfield.

Pitts tied for second in receptions and targets for the Falcons on the afternoon, but he averaged just 4.4 yards per catch. However, the veteran tight end did score for the third consecutive game, recording a five-yard touchdown catch with just under nine minutes remaining in the third quarter. Pitts' production will inevitably fluctuate week to week, but he's clearly established himself as a reliable red-zone target for Michael Penix heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday.

Penix put together a solid, mistake-free effort that saw him toss a trio of touchdown passes for the second straight game. The 2024 first-round pick connected with Nick Muse (one yard), Kyle Pitts (five yards) and Drake London (21 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, the latter two coming in the second half. Penix also completed over 71.0 percent of his passes for the third time in five games this season, and he'll take an excellent 9:1 TD:INT and 1,157 passing yards into a Week 8 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday.

Ioane suffered a sprained MCL in his right knee in Week 7 versus the Bengals, and he was initially expected to miss time. It now looks possible that he could be available as Sunday versus the Bills, but he will receive an official injury designation after Friday's final practice of the week.

Tampa had his 21-day practice window opened by Baltimore last week, and Thursday marked his first full practice. The cornerback has been on injured reserve since mid-September with a knee injury, but he appears to be closing in on a return to action.

Washington missed Baltimore's past two contests due to an ankle injury. He opened this week with a limited practice, but with a full session under his belt Thursday, he should be able to return to action this Sunday. Washington has worked in a rotational role this season, logging between a 23 percent and 39 percent defensive snap share in each of his five games.

Stanley has dealt with a toe injury much of the season, and he missed Week 3 due to the issue. He was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, but with a full session one day later, the veteran offensive tackle should be good to go for Sunday's Week 8 clash in Buffalo.

Smith didn't practice Wednesday. However, he logged a limited session Thursday, so he's trending in the right direction toward being available for Sunday's game against the Bills. The 29-year-old has appeared in all seven regular-season games for the Ravens, accumulating 55 total tackles (24 solo), 2.0 sacks and one interception.

Hamilton was injured during the Week 7 loss to Cincinnati. He didn't practice Wednesday and was observed wearing a brace on his right knee. Although the 25-year-old was a limited participant in Thursday's session, he should still be considered questionable for Sunday's game versus Buffalo. If Hamilton can't suit up, Keondre Jackson, Keyon Martin and K'Von Wallace are candidates for more snaps.

Jackson seems on track to return to action for Sunday's game at Buffalo after logging back-to-back uncapped sessions to begin Week 8 prep. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if he's tagged with a designation for that matchup, but the quarterback is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a left high-ankle sprain.

Hawkins has now been held out of four consecutive practices due to the knee issue and could be trending toward missing a second straight game Sunday in Buffalo. If Hawkins ends up being sidelined against the Bills, Keondre Jackson and K'Von Wallace would be in line for extra snaps alongside starting safety Malaki Starks.

Randall was a full participant in his return to practice. The Ravens placed the running back on IR in late August with an undisclosed injury, which has now been revealed to be a neck issue. Randall's instant jump to full participation means the fifth-round rookie could be ready to suit up as soon as Sunday's game against the Bills.
questionable

Cuevas connected with Tyler Huntley on a 16-yard pass on the Ravens' first offensive play of the game, but the duo didn't find each other again until late in the third quarter on a 19-yarder. Cuevas had only one catch for 14 yards through the first four games of the regular season, but the rookie fifth-rounder has an 8-105-1 line on 10 targets over his last three outings. That coincides with Huntley being under center, but the Ravens are expecting Lamar Jackson (ankle) to return for Week 8 against the Bills on Nov. 1.

Lane finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Zay Flowers (11), and he was able to reel in at least three passes for the second straight week. With Lamar Jackson (ankle) nearing a return to action, Lane may be able to establish himself as a reliable red-zone threat for Baltimore moving forward this season. The rookie's next chance to record his first career touchdown will come in Week 8 versus the Bills.

Baltimore led for most of the game Sunday before falling behind late in the third quarter, and from that point on, the game script favored Hill. Even still, his snap count at running back in Week 7 (29) lagged behind that of starter Derrick Henry (33). When Lamar Jackson (ankle) returns to action, it should give a boost to the entire Ravens offense.

Bateman was able to handle a full workload for the first time since Week 5 after dealing with a shoulder injury, and the wide receiver was on the field for 74 percent of the team's offensive snaps. He finished tied for third on the team in targets with running back Justice Hill and tight end Mark Andrews, and Bateman's 33 receiving yards ranked third. The wide receiver and the rest of the team's pass catchers would stand to see an increase in production if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is able to return to action in Week 8 versus Buffalo.

Andrews reeled in three or fewer passes for the second straight game and third time overall this season, and he has now gone five games in a row without recording 30-plus receiving yards. The tight end's production will likely go up once Lamar Jackson (ankle) is able to return, but he no longer appears to be a must-roster asset in fantasy football. Through seven games this season, Andrews has caught 26 of 37 targets for 204 yards and one touchdown.

Huntley had the Ravens seemingly in control through two quarters, when he helped stake Baltimore to a 13-0 halftime lead by tossing a 48-yard touchdown pass to Zay Flowers in the first quarter. The veteran signal-caller couldn't lead his squad to any second-half points, however, but because Huntley had to continue throwing as Cincinnati built its lead, he finished with a career-high single-game yardage total. Huntley has put together a 4:1 TD:INT over three starts in Lamar Jackson's (ankle) stead, but it's likely the latter will be able to suit up in next Sunday's Week 8 road showdown against the Bills.

Loop made an extra point in the first quarter and field goals from 34 and 24 yards in the second quarter before he and the rest of the Ravens went scoreless in the second half.  The kicker has now gone 12-for-15 on field-goal tries while converting all 17 of his PATs over the first seven contests during the 2026 campaign.

Henry averaged below 3.5 yards per carry for the second consecutive game against a divisional opponent, and Sunday's inefficiency also dropped his season per-carry average under 4.0 (3.9). The bruising back does have seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but none have come within the last three games. Henry will look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 8 road showdown against an improved Bills run defense next Sunday.

The standout receiver had a big hand in staking the Ravens to a 13-0 halftime lead, and although Baltimore couldn't muster a single point in the second half, Flowers still finished with team-high reception, receiving yardage and target totals. Flowers also had a game-long 48-yard catch, which qualified as his third touchdown of the season. Flowers has shown excellent chemistry with both Lamar Jackson (ankle) and Tyler Huntley, and reports indicate the fleet-footed receiver is likely to have the former under center for a Week 8 road showdown against the Bills.

injuries.evidence: Robinson suffered a season-ending pectoral injury during the Ravens' Week 6 loss to the Browns.
injuries.detail: Robinson suffered a season-ending pectoral injury during the Ravens' Week 6 loss to the Browns. The outside linebacker will spend the rest of 2026 on IR, allowing the Ravens to carry more depth on the offensive line. The team signed offensive guard Kyle Hergel from the practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move.

Jurgens has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and has been cleared to play in Sunday's contest. The center was acquired via a trade with the Eagles while he still had his concussion, sidelining him for his first two games with the Ravens. While Jurgens is set to suit up, starting quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) may need to wait until Week 8 to play with his new starting center.

Hibner managed a full practice Thursday for the first time since he hurt his hand back in Week 5 at Atlanta, suggesting he'll more than likely be available in Week 7 versus the Bengals. Before getting hurt, he was operating as Baltimore's secondary tight end, filling a complementary role relative to veteran starter Mark Andrews.
reserve-sus

Oliver made his return to practice Wednesday after missing the team's two most recent contests with a knee injury, but he now appears to be good to go for Week 8. The defensive lineman has recorded nine total tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, while also recovering a fumble over three contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Kincaid has started Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practice sessions coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. The 27-year-old TE has yet to miss a game this season, but Kincaid has cooled down significantly after a scorching start, mustering 90 receiving yards over the past four games after posting 225 yards and a TD through Week 2. Kincaid will look to get back on track Sunday against the Ravens, assuming he plays through the chest injury that's limiting his practice participation.

Moore has been listed as limited both Wednesday and Thursday while practicing in a non-contact jersey. The 29-year-old wide receiver missed Buffalo's last two games prior to a Week 7 bye after having appeared in 92 consecutive regular-season games. Keon Coleman stepped up in Moore's absence and could maintain a larger role Sunday against the Ravens if Moore is ultimately sidelined or limited.
questionable

Davis received the day off while he was feeling under the weather, but so long as he's able to get back on the practice field Friday, he should avoid taking a designation into Sunday's game against the Ravens. While handling a backup role behind lead back James Cook this season, Davis has carried just five times for 12 yards to go with three receptions for 40 yards through Buffalo's first six contests.

Shavers has progressed enough in his recovery from a torn ACL to return to practice, and he was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Shavers saw his role in the Bills' offense steadily increase over the course of the 2025 season before suffering his injury in the wild-card round against the Jaguars in January. His next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Vikings on Monday, Nov. 9.

Franklin was disciplined by the league for allegedly spitting at an opponent late in the fourth quarter of the Bills' Week 6 win over the Raiders. The decision has been altered to a fine, and with the Bills on a bye, the Temple product will be available for Week 8 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Despite a relatively poor showing from a struggling Bills defense, Williams picked off Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The linebacker's stolen possession, the first interception of his NFL career, led to the Bills extending the lead from 16-13 to 23-13 with 6:22 remaining in the third quarter.

Igbinosun, a second-round rookie out of Ohio State, has seen 64 or more percent of the defensive snaps in each of the past three games as he continues to make his mark at the NFL level. That's more than teammate Maxwell Hairston in each of the past two, so IGB may be working his way into a starter's role opposite star corner Christian Benford. Igbinosun had seven total tackles in Week 6, and he had three passes defensed in the Week 7 win over the Raiders.

He again played about as many snaps at tight end Sunday (47) as did starter Dalton Kincaid (49), but Knox continued to function mostly as a blocker. He has yet to draw more than three targets in a game this season, and he'll probably remain on the periphery of the passing offense as long as Kincaid is still available.

Bass was dominant during the victory, as he was perfect on all of his kicks. The 29-year-old continues to have a strong season, as he has missed just two kicks (both PATs) across his first six appearances.

Johnson and Ray Davis each saw only one carry during Sunday's win, with lead back James Cook turning 22 carries into 95 yards and a touchdown. Johnson was still involved somewhat in the passing game, and through four games he has 12 catches on as many targets for 155 yards. The veteran running back will continue to operate in a rotational role on offense, but his workload would expand significantly if Cook ever misses time. The Bills are on a bye for Week 7, and their next game will take place in Week 8 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Palmer was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and his 17 offensive snaps were last among the Bills' active wide receivers with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. Palmer connected with Josh Allen on a 37-yard pass late in the first quarter to move the Bills into opposing territory, leading to a 28-yard field goal by Tyler Bass nine plays later. Three of Palmer's four catches this season have gone for 30-plus yards, but he isn't a featured part of the Bills'offense and will see his role decrease once Moore is cleared to return. Buffalo is on a bye for Week 7 and will return to action for Week 8 against Baltimore on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Coleman led the Bills in receiving yards on the afternoon with the help of a 21-yard grab and a 12-yard touchdown reception with just over six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The score was Coleman's third of the season, with the previous two having come in each of the prior pair of contests against the Patriots and Rams. The oft-maligned 2024 second-round pick appears to be picking up some momentum in his third season, as Coleman already has a 19-283-3 line on 24 targets while helping make up for the multiple absences of DJ Moore (shoulder).

Shakir posted his second-lowest yardage figure of the season, but the talented veteran recorded his first touchdown of the campaign on a nine-yard grab just past the midway point of the second quarter. His target total also tied for his second highest of the campaign, a figure he'd reached on two other occasions. The fifth-year pro should continue to garner his fair share of Josh Allen's attention moving forward, although Shakir's targets could take a slight hit if DJ Moore (shoulder) returns for a Week 8 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

Allen once again operated without DJ Moore (shoulder), although he did have another deep threat in Joshua Palmer back from his own shoulder issue. The one-time MVP signal-caller spread the ball around to eight different targets, and Allen ultimately played without Dalton Kincaid (rib) for a spell in the second half as well. Allen's passing numbers haven't been particularly impressive since a 334-yard showing against the Texans back in Week 1 as first-year head coach Joe Brady looks to run a balanced attack. However, the prolific quarterback still has 1,504 passing yards with a 9:4 TD:INT and another 240 rushing yards and eight additional scores going into a Week 8 home showdown with the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

Lee was hurt in the first half and was deemed doubtful to return shortly before halftime. In the expected event that Lee can't re-enter the contest, Marco Wilson and Malcolm DeWalt will likely handled much of the cornerback snaps for Carolina.

injuries.evidence: The 27-year-old will now be forced to miss at least four games while on IR, and in his absence, Will Lee, Malcolm DeWalt and Chau Smith-Wade will stand to operate as the team's primary options at cornerback.
injuries.detail: Evans is dealing with a triceps injury, and he was unable to practice at all this week ahead of being ruled out for Thursday night's contest versus Green Bay. The 27-year-old will now be forced to miss at least four games while on IR, and in his absence, Will Lee, Malcolm DeWalt and Chau Smith-Wade will stand to operate as the team's primary options at cornerback.
Brown will be forced to miss Week 8 as he nurses an apparent hand injury. In his absence, Aaron Hall and TeRah Edwards are both candidates to see an increase in workload on Carolina's defensive line.

King will once again serve as the team's emergency QB for the seventh game in a row. The rookie would only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Bryce Young and primary backup Kenny Pickett are forced out of the contest.
Sanders will be a healthy scratch for the sixth game in a row to open the regular season. Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller will operate as the team's primary options at tight end versus the Packers.

Dillon will be a healthy scratch for the second straight week as the Panthers go with Chuba Hubbard, Trevor Etienne and Anthony Tyus as their three options in the backfield. Dillon appears to have found himself far down the pecking order, and he is unlikely to be a major part of Carolina's future plans.

Simpkins was unable to practice all week due to an ankle injury, which he likely picked up during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers. With Damien Lewis (knee) also ruled out, Corey Bullock will likely start at left guard in Thursday night's game. Simpkins' next chance to suit up is Week 9 against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Lewis likely picked up the injury during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers. He was unable to practice all week due to his injury, and with Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) also ruled out, Corey Bullock figures to step into the starting role at left guard. Lewis' next chance to play is Week 9 against the Broncos on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Phillips did not practice at all during the Panthers' Week 8 prep. The linebacker aggravated a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Eagles and continues to pay the price. It is unclear whether Phillips is tracking to return to practice ahead of Week 9 or will need to miss even more time due to the injury.

Lloyd had a pretty quiet game, as the four stops tied his lowest mark of the campaign. He logged at least nine tackles in each of his first three contests, so he'll likely perk up his tackle production soon. Lloyd had been quite productive this season as a whole, as he's recorded 2.0 sacks and two interceptions, one of which he returned for a touchdown.

Okereke paced the Panthers in stops during a tough day for the team's defense, as Tampa Bay cruised to a 43-13 win. The veteran linebacker reached the double-digit tackle mark for the first time this season, and he's posted six or more stops in five of his six games. On the season, Okereke leads Carolina with 44 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, and has added five defensed passes (including one interception) and one forced fumble.

After being listed as limited in Monday's practice estimate, Coker was able to take a step forward in activity a day later. With a full practice under his belt, Coker should be ready to handle his usual snap share in Thursday's game against the Packers. Coker -- who was held to one reception on four targets in Week 7 -- and the rest of the passing attack will look to bounce back after Carolina quarterbacks Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett were limited to just 178 yards through the air in a 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.

Metchie caught two passes for the third time this season. While the 26-year-old could be on the field more if there are injuries within the receiving corps moving ahead, he still isn't anticipated to be a week-to-week fantasy producer.

Evans logged more offensive snaps than Darren Waller for the third consecutive contest. However, despite the increased involvement, it was another unproductive effort from the 23-year-old, who now has just eight catches for 105 yards in six regular-season games in 2026.

Etienne made his second appearance of the 2026 campaign after missing the first four games due to an ankle injury. Although he was slightly more productive than he was in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, it was still an underwhelming showing overall. Etienne should continue to occupy the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. However, Chuba Hubbard is anticipated to nearly monopolize the touches out of the backfield moving forward, leaving sparse opportunity for anyone else.

Tremble had two touchdowns in the 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6. However, it was a different story in Week 7, with the 26-year-old catching just one pass for the second time this season. While Tremble could find the end zone again at some point moving forward, he likely won't be consistent enough to be considered anything other than a desperation fantasy option, especially while Darren Waller is on the field.

Moton fractured his fibula in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. The offensive tackle will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season due to the injury, making the move to injured reserve a formality. Monroe Freeling is set to start at right tackle for the Panthers for the remainder of the season.

With Carolina getting smeared on the scoreboard late in the game, the Panthers pulled their starters, and Tyus got some run on offense. He scored a 12-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Tyus isn't even remotely on the fantasy radar while Chuba Hubbard is healthy.

Fitzgerald went without a field-goal attempt for the first time in his two-year career, and to make matters worse, he registered his fifth missed PAT of the season. The kicker has now gone 11-for-11 on field-goal tries while converting 12 of 17 extra-point attempts over six regular-season contests this year.

Waller's one catch not only netted Bryce Young his only passing touchdown of the day, but it also generated team-high receiving yardage. The veteran tight end's splash play naturally was a boon for his fantasy managers, but Waller has seen just four targets over the last two games after opening the season with multiple catches in each of the first four contests. Waller will take a 14-198-3 line into a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday.

Young's performance was a microcosm of the Panthers' day as a whole, as the 2023 first overall pick posted a season-low passing yardage tally and completed under 52.0 percent of his passes for the second straight game. Young also tossed multiple picks for the first time this season, and the two miscues led to 10 total points for Tampa Bay. The entire afternoon was essentially a throwaway game for Carolina, and Young and his teammates will look to quickly rebound in a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday night.

Hubbard did well with the scant opportunities he received, but his touches were limited in a game that was already out of reach by halftime. The veteran back's rush attempts and rushing yardage were both season lows, and the downturn came on the heels of back-to-back 120-plus-yard efforts for Hubbard on the ground. The 2021 fourth-round pick won't have to wait long to atone for Sunday's quiet game, as the Panthers face off with the Packers on Thursday in a Week 8 road matchup.

Edwards was forced to miss the team's last two games while nursing a hamstring injury, but he appears to be on track to return to action in Week 8. The linebacker will have two more chances to officially log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Seahawks.

Monangai hasn't suited up since Week 4, and he continues to be bothered by a pair of injures at the start of Chicago's Week 8 prep. He'll have an extra day to recover with the Bears playing on MNF against Seattle. Roschon Johnson has played in a change-of-pace role behind D'Andre Swift during Monangai's absence.

Chicago parted with a hefty package of draft picks to land the standout defensive tackle from the 1-6 Titans. Simmons had a career-high 11.0 sacks in 15 appearances last season and is slightly behind that pace this season, with 4.0 sacks through seven games. The four-time Pro Bowler has four passes defensed and 38.0 tackles (20 solo) this season. He'll likely make his Bears debut Monday against the Seahawks.

Johnson said that Bryant's timeline for return is still indefinite, but it looks like a possibility he could be back on the field as soon as December or January. He is recovering from a knee surgery he underwent back in August after he suffered a hyperextension during training camp. Per Cronin, he is still on a four- to six-month timeline to return.

Scott was elevated each of the past three weeks, so this was a necessary move for him to be eligible to continue suiting up on game days. The 27-year-old has been providing depth at running back in the absence of Kyle Monangai (toe), who has been sidelined for each of the three contests that Scott has been elevated. With that said, Scott has yet to log an offensive snap this season, so he's unlikely to be a factor on offense in Week 8 versus Seattle even if Monangai is absent again.

Gordon's sack came early -- he brought down Drake Maye for a loss of one yard on a fourth-down play during the Patriots' first offensive drive. The star cornerback has been a terror for opposing offenses through his first two games, as he's already blown by his previous career high with 4.0 sacks. Gordon has done that despite playing a modest 48 defensive snaps across the two contests. He upped his snap share to 58 percent Thursday (after posting a 31 percent mark in his season debut Week 6) and should continue to increase his time on the field as he moves further past a calf injury.

Thieneman's eight stops led the Bears. The rookie safety also got to the quarterback for a second straight game, as he was credited with a half-sack of Drake Maye in the fourth quarter. Thieneman has already established himself as a viable IDP asset, posting at least six tackles in six of seven contests and recording 1.5 sacks along with an interception through seven games.

Roush didn't catch a pass against New England on Thursday, marking his third straight game without a reception. However, he's currently the only healthy tight end on the Bears' roster aside from starter Colston Loveland, so Roush figures to be in line for an expanded role moving forward. With that said, Loveland has logged 57 or more receiving yards and six or more catches three of the past four weeks and is clearly the Bears' go-to tight end in the passing game, so Roush's anticipated increase of offensive snaps doesn't necessarily make him a viable option in fantasy.

Raymond started at WR for Chicago and got plenty of playing time, logging 48 of 69 snaps on offense. However, he was unable to make an impact, finishing without a catch for the first time this season. Top wideouts Luther Burden and Rome Odunze combined for eight catches, 199 yards and a touchdown Thursday, and Raymond figures to compete for scraps whenever that pair is healthy.

Johnson played just 10 offensive snaps to D'Andre Swift's 54 in the contest. The running back did not see much action as he filled in for the injured Kyle Monangai (toe) as a rotational option for the Bears' offense. Johnson also saw one snap with the special teams unit.

The defensive end is set to return to practice in Week 8 and should play in the team's Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks. Sweat has logged seven tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his five regular-season appearances so far in 2026.

injuries.evidence: Kmet suffered a season-ending right knee injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
injuries.detail: Kmet suffered a season-ending right knee injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday. Even with the emergence of Colston Loveland, Kmet was still a key piece in Chicago's offense as a run blocker, and he'll end his 2026 regular season with a 10-87-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) across seven games. Rookie third-rounder Sam Roush is the only other healthy tight end on the 53-man roster other than Loveland, so the Bears could look to bolster the position group by trade or free agency.

Odunze was encouragingly efficient in the high-scoring win, but he once again saw fellow wideout Luther Burden be more productive. Burden's 130 receiving yards led the Bears on the night, and Odunze appears to have fallen into more of a de facto No. 2 role at this point in the season. Odunze still carries solid fantasy value, however, and he'll carry a 24-381-0 line on 38 targets into a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

The second-year tight end continued to shake out of his early-season slump, putting together his second fantasy-friendly performance in a five-day span. Loveland led the Bears in receptions and targets on the night with figures that also qualified as season highs, and he added his second touchdown in five days on a 12-yard grab early in the third quarter. He has a 13-134-2 line in the last two games alone and should continue playing a key role in a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2, and he could be in line for even heavier involvement if Cole Kmet (knee) is unable to suit up.

Santos put the first points on the board with a 43-yard field goal in the first quarter and added a 31-yarder in the second. He had a chance to give Chicago a two-score lead midway through the fourth quarter but clanged a 53-yard attempt off the right upright. However, Santos atoned for that miss in dramatic fashion, knocking in a 58-yard field goal -- the longest make of his career -- with less than two minutes remaining to essentially seal the win for the Bears. He's now 11-for-15 on field-goal tries this season, including 3-for-5 from 50-plus yards.

With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out for a third straight game, Swift once again handled a workhorse role and parlayed it into some solid production. Swift's rushing yardage total was his third highest of the season, and the veteran back got into the end zone for the third straight game on a four-yard run late in the first quarter. He's up to seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but his touches will take a hit if Monangai is able to get healthy enough over the extended time between Thursday's game and a Week 8 road matchup against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2 to suit up for that contest.

Burden comfortably led the Bears in receiving yards with the second-highest total of his career, and he added his second touchdown catch of the season on a 24-yard grab just before halftime. He also had a game-long 58-yard catch late in the first quarter to set up a D'Andre Swift four-yard touchdown one play later, and the fleet-footed receiver has accumulated 225 of his 491 receiving yards on the season in the last two games alone. Burden has arguably overtaken Rome Odunze as Chicago's most explosive pass-catching weapon, and he should play a critical role again in a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

Williams spearheaded another prolific performance for the Bears offense, leading his squad to another 30-point tally while eclipsing the 300-yard mark for the second time in five days. He tied his season high with 9.3 yards per attempt, and he accomplished his stellar numbers while focusing on a tight pool of five targets. The 2024 first overall pick's two touchdown passes went to Luther Burden (24 yards) and Colston Loveland (12 yards), marking Williams' first multi-TD tally since Week 1. Williams appears to be clicking on all cylinders in his second season in head coach Ben Johnson's aggressive offense, now having completed 71.0 percent of his passes for 1,020 yards through four games heading into a Week 8 road showdown with the defending champion Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

Muhammad is dealing with a toe injury, and he will now likely be forced to watch the remainder of the game from the Bears' sideline. In Muhammad's absence, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips are both candidates to see an increase in workload at cornerback.

Iosivas has been on injured reserve since Sept. 26 while recovering from a torn ligament in his left thumb that required surgery. The wide receiver is reportedly on track to be available to play in Week 10 against the Steelers, and he has an outside chance of returning one week prior against the Falcons in Spain on Nov. 8, per Petraglia.

After sitting out Wednesday's session, Chase assuaged any concerns regarding his availability for Sunday's game against the Titans by practicing without limitations Thursday. The star wide receiver will look to pick up the pace following what has been a slow start by his lofty standards. Chase is averaging a career-low 58.5 receiving yards per game after notching at least 76 yards per game in each of the previous five regular seasons.

All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

Carter didn't play every defensive snap for just the first time this season, but his nine stops were tied with Bryan Cook for most on the Bengals. Carter has logged at least five stops in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 50 tackles (22 solo), including 1.5 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble in 2026.

Mafe got to Tyler Huntley for a six-yard sack midway through the first quarter before splitting another sack with Bryan Cook in the fourth. Mafe has logged at least 1.0 sacks in three consecutive games and is up to 4.5 sacks through six regular-season games, which already surpasses his total from 2025 with Seattle (2.0 sacks across 17 regular-season contests).

Cook and Boye Mafe combined for a split sack on Tyler Huntley midway through the fourth quarter, which was Cook's first sack since his rookie year in 2022. The fifth-year safety is up to 26 tackles (18 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through five regular-season games.

Knight finished third on the team in tackles behind Bryan Cook and Barrett Carter during the victory, in addition to snagging his first interception of the campaign. The 26-year-old continues to have a productive season, as he's now recorded seven or more tackles in five of his six appearances, bringing his total on the campaign to 50 (21 solo).

With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both fully healthy, Meyers played just 20 of 53 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on Joe Burrow's 32 dropbacks. Outside of his 7-82-0 receiving performance in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Meyers has totaled six catches for 59 yards in the other five games.

Dugger was injured in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens and did not return. The 30-year-old will now miss at least one game, and while there will likely be more updates on his health moving forward, he should be considered week-to-week. Dugger hasn't seen consistent action on the defensive side of the ball, though his absence will be felt on special teams.

Grandy spent the previous two seasons with Cincinnati prior to being a part of final cuts this past summer. With Tanner Hudson (pectoral) done for the season and Erick All going down with a knee injury Sunday against the Ravens, Grandy gives the Bengals another reliable tight end behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample.

Gesicki isn't seeing reliable volume in the form of targets, but he's been a big factor in the red zone this season, as he now has five touchdowns in six games. He's already one away from matching his career high, which was set in 2020 with the Dolphins. Gesicki is repping as the Bengals' slot receiver between Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but the latter two dominate the passing looks from Joe Burrow.

The running back wasn't targeted in the passing game, but Perine notably subbed in for Chase Brown at the goal line to punch in a one-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter. It's become apparent that the coaches are trusting Perine more, and it's having an effect on Brown's production. Perine is up to 31 carries for 126 yards (4.1 YPC) and one touchdown through six games this season.

Sample entered Week 7 with just five catches for 24 yards on six targets across five games, so he doubled his yardage total and secured his first touchdown with Sunday's performance. It goes without saying, but Sample isn't on the fantasy football radar.

Brown didn't partake in the Bengals' five-touchdown second-half explosion, but the versatile back had a serviceable day on a per-touch basis. However, Brown hasn't really come close to reaching the 100-yard mark on the ground in any game this season -- the closest he's come is 80 yards -- and he's been at 61 yards or fewer in five of six contests. Brown's pass-catching work continues to typically be plentiful, but he still has a relatively modest outlook heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

McPherson and the rest of the Bengals were blanked before halftime, but the kicker was able to finish off five touchdown drives in the second half. McPherson has now attempted one or zero field goals in three straight games after opening the season with multiple field-goal makes in each of the team's first three contests.

Burrow couldn't lead the Bengals to a single point in the first half, but the 2020 first overall pick came out of intermission locked in. He helped spearhead five consecutive scoring drives to start the second half, capping four of them with touchdown passes to Mike Gesicki (six yards), Tee Higgins (13 yards), Ja'Marr Chase (two yards ) and Drew Sample (16 yards). The game marked Burrow's second straight with four scoring tosses and zero interceptions, and both his passing yardage total and 73.3 percent completion rate were his second highest of the season. He'll take 1,653 passing yards and a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

The Bengals' air attack as a whole got off to a very sluggish start, leading to a scoreless first half. However, Cincinnati exploded for 35 points after intermission, and Higgins played a big role by posting team-high reception and receiving yardage totals while tying for the team lead in targets. The veteran wideout also recorded his second touchdown catch of the campaign on a 13-yard grab with just under five minutes remaining in the third quarter that gave Cincinnati a 14-13 lead. Higgins is averaging an outstanding 17.3 yards per reception on a 33-571-2 receiving line heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

Young missed each of the Bengals' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a knee injury. The extra rest has paid dividends for the rookie fourth-rounder, who is on track to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown against the Ravens. He's operated in a minimal role offensively this season, having logged only two catches on as many targets for nine yards across three games.

Sampson was limited in the Browns' first practice of the week, but he was likely just having his reps managed after he had missed five straight games due to the knee injury before returning to action during this past Sunday's win over the Titans. With a full practice now under his belt, Sampson is in the clear to serve as the top change-of-pace option behind lead back Quinshon Judkins in this weekend's game against the Steelers.

Howard is in the league's concussion protocol after exiting Sunday's win over the Titans due to a concussion. Dawand Jones is in line to start at right tackle if Howard is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Sunday's matchup versus the Steelers.

Hall has missed the Browns' past three games because of a lingering ankle injury, and now his status for Week 8 is in jeopardy. He'll likely need to practice in full Thursday or Friday to not go into the weekend with an injury designation.

Harden hurt his hamstring during Sunday's game at Tennessee, and now his availability for Week 8 is in question. He'll probably have to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram, coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that he gave Verse the day off and expects him to play Sunday at Pittsburgh. With that said, his activity at practice Thursday and Friday might still be worth keeping an eye on.

The rookie wide receiver duo of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, along with second-year tight end Harold Fannin, have dominated most of the targets from quarterback Deshaun Watson. Jeudy has been less involved offensively, although he's had a slight uptick in work of late, accumulating 14 catches (on 18 targets) for 145 yards over his last four games. The 2020 first-rounder brings a veteran presence to the Browns' pass-catching group, but given his lower workload compared to his younger teammates in Cleveland, Jeudy could garner interest from a team who is in more need of depth at wide receiver.

Schwesinger finished third on the Browns in tackles Sunday behind both Quincy Williams and Ronnie Hickman (10 each). Schwesinger has played every single defensive snap through seven regular-season games and has logged at least eight stops in six of those contests. He's up to 64 total tackles on the year, which leads the Browns and is sixth-most in the NFL.

Hickman and Quincy Williams co-led the Browns in tackles Sunday, with the former playing every defensive snap for the sixth time this season. Hickman's 10 tackles were his most of the season, and the fourth-year safety is up to 41 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and two fumble recoveries through seven regular-season contests.

Williams was working through neck and back injuries during Week 7 prep, but he was cleared to play Sunday and ended up playing every single defensive snap while co-leading the Browns in tackles with Ronnie Hickman. It was the second time in three games that Williams recorded double-digit stops, and he is up to 50 tackles (30 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses and three forced fumbles through seven regular-season contests.

Davis injured his quad during training camp in late July and started the regular season on IR. His 21-day window opened Oct. 6, but he has not progressed enough in his recovery to warrant his removal from IR. That means that the 2022 sixth-rounder will be sidelined for the rest of the season unless he reaches an injury settlement with the Browns.

McLaughlin played a key role in the Browns' Week 6 win over the Ravens, when he had nine carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all four of his targets for 13 yards. However, his role on offense evaporated Sunday due to the returns of both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. McLaughlin figures to be limited to return duties moving forward unless one or both of Judkins or Sampson misses time.

Cleveland needed to make a decision on the quarterback after opening his 21-day practice window 20 days ago, so he'll now join the 53-man roster as one of the team's four quarterbacks. The Browns figure to make a move at the position in the near future, and perhaps they'll try to gauge trade interest in Gabriel.

The wide receiver was the favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year after the first five weeks of the season, but he's now posted back-to-back subpar games against the Ravens and Titans. During those two contests, Boston has four catches for 42 yards on 13 targets. He's been extremely inefficient with his looks and isn't getting loose for big plays over the top of the defense. He'll try to get back on track next Sunday in Pittsburgh.

The second-year tight end delivered a season high in receiving yards, and Fannin's last catch was his biggest. With the game tied at 24-24 in the final minute of the fourth quarter, Fannin took a short pass over the middle from Deshaun Watson and tacked on about 30 yards after the catch to set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. Fannin will take a 25-257-3 line on 39 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Steelers.

While he didn't throw a TD pass for a second straight game, Watson produced a season high in passing yards and scored his first rushing TD since Week 2 of the 2024 season on a nine-yard scamper in the fourth quarter. Watson also led his fifth game-winning, fourth-quarter drive of the year, completing another comeback after the Browns fell behind 14-0 early. The veteran QB will take a 7:3 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 meeting with the Steelers.

The rookie wideout put together a breakout performance, with his 10 targets, eight catches and 129 receiving yards all being season highs. If fact, the yardage total was more than Concepcion had produced in any two of his first six NFL games combined. Concepcion's chemistry with Deshaun Watson is growing, and he'll be hunting for his first career touchdown in Week 8 against the Steelers.

Williams was also labeled as limited for Wednesday's walkthrough, so the hamstring issue isn't entirely preventing him from practicing. Still, the veteran defender will likely get tagged with a designation for Sunday's matchup against Arizona if he's not able to upgrade to full participation Friday. Williams has been an important part of the Cowboys' pass rush of late, logging a sack in three of his past four games.

Downs was deemed limited Wednesday as well, though that was a walkthrough. With an actual limited practice under his belt Thursday, the rookie defender seems to have a decent chance of playing Sunday against Arizona. Downs has taken on a near every-down role as a rookie, playing every defensive snap in five of his seven games so far.

Winters suffered a calf injury in Week 6 against Green Bay and hasn't practiced since. He's likely trending toward missing Sunday's Week 8 matchup against Arizona, though the veteran linebacker could give himself a chance to suit up in that contest if he's able to practice in some capacity Friday. Should Winters miss another game, however, Shemar James would likely start in his place.

Turpin was also a DNP on Wednesday, though that was a walkthrough. The Cowboys held a standard practice Thursday, and Turpin was unable to participate, casting doubt on his availability for Sunday's game against Arizona. Still, Turpin will have a chance to log at least a limited session Friday ahead of the weekend.

Bullard had his 21-day practice window opened Thursday, and the defensive lineman logged a full practice, per Todd Archer of ESPN.com. The 33-year-old has been sidelined since suffering a calf injury in Week 3. It's unclear if Bullard will be good to go for Week 8, but he doesn't appear to be too far away from a return to action.

Pickens is dealing with a lingering shoulder issue and a new hamstring injury, which so far has capped his practice reps this week. He'll have one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Cowboys may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

Aubrey benefited from a bounce-back performance out of Dallas' offense, as he had been limited to one field-goal attempt and two PATs over the previous two games combined. Monday marked the third time Aubrey made three field goals in a game this season, as he connected from 55, 27 and 24 yards. Aubrey's likely to remain busy in Week 8 against the Cardinals, who are giving up a league-high 29.7 points per game.

Overshown was given the green light by medical staff to play Monday after missing the Cowboys' five previous games due to a hamstring injury. The fourth-year linebacker ended up co-leading Dallas in tackles and he picked off Tanner McKee midway through the fourth quarter. Overshown has played in only 21 regular-season games since being selected by the Cowboys in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft, but he's still a key piece in the defense when healthy.

Monday was the first time since Week 8 of the 2025 season that Ferguson failed to record a catch, and the only pass he saw from Dak Prescott was on a broken play in the red zone early in the fourth quarter. Ferguson's 38 offensive snaps were only two more than fellow tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford, and the latter's role in the offense has grown over the last few weeks at the expense of the former. Week 8 against the Cardinals presents itself as a bounce-back opportunity for Ferguson, seeing as Arizona's defense ranks 27th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to tight ends.

The Cowboys relied heavily on the run game Monday, and Goodson saw a season-high 10 rushes as a result, although that was still well behind the workload of lead back Javonte Williams, who turned 25 carries into a career-high 155 yards and a score. Goodson nearly found the end zone himself after returning a 91-yard kickoff to the house in the second quarter, only for the touchdown to be nullified by a holding penalty on Dallas. He's limited to RB2 duties for the time being but would step into an elevated role if Williams were to ever miss time. The Cowboys will head back home for Week 8 against the Cardinals, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (126.4).

With the Cowboys opening the game in 12 personnel, Spann-Ford was credited with a start and was on the field for 36 of the team's 68 offensive snaps on the night (52.9 percent). Though Jake Ferguson is locked in as Dallas' top tight end, Spann-Ford has consistently repped ahead of Luke Schoonmaker as the No. 2 option at the position since Week 2. While he's mainly functioned as a blocker, Spann-Ford has been a solid complementary option in the passing game with a 9-79-0 line on 13 targets.

Flournoy tied with George Pickens for second in receptions and outgained his teammate by 13 receiving yards to finish as the runner-up in that category as well. The second-year wideout has popped for 90- and 70-yard tallies in two of his last three games, and although his week-to-week production remains somewhat erratic, Flournoy does have some upside thanks to his growing chemistry with Dak Prescott.

Williams broke out for a new single-game career high in rushing yards during the impressive victory, sealing the win with a two-yard scoring run just ahead of the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The remarkable performance also marked Williams' first 100-yard tally of the season, and he's been highly rewarding for fantasy managers by scoring a touchdown in five straight games. Williams should have a prime opportunity to continue building on his strong first half of the season in Week 8, as he'll face a vulnerable Cardinals run defense at home on Sunday.

The Cowboys were able to keep Prescott upright throughout the night, and the veteran signal-caller leveraged the solid protection into his first multi-touchdown-pass tally since Week 2. Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb (nine, 16 yards) and George Pickens (21 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and although his 55.6 percent completion rate was a season low, Prescott was able to steer clear of interceptions after throwing two apiece in Weeks 5 and 6. Prescott now has 1,851 passing yards and a 13:5 TD:INT going into a favorable Week 8 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Lamb led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth and sixth touchdowns of the season on nine- and 16-yard scoring grabs. The veteran star has 70 or more receiving yards in two straight and five of his last six contests overall, and Lamb's average of 11.6 targets per game gives him an elite floor heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Locke's 21-day practice window opened Friday, and he was a limited participant in each of the last two practices of Week 7 prep. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a foot injury, but he's not quite ready to be activated from IR. His next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Liufau was designated to return from injured reserve Thursday and was a full practice participant Friday and Saturday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag, but the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery from a broken left forearm. Given his ability to practice without restrictions, Liufau has a good chance of being activated from IR for Week 8 against the Cardinals on Nov. 1.

Durant was a full practice participant Friday and Saturday, and that was enough for the fifth-year defensive back to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. His presence gives the Cowboys another contributor on special teams and depth in the secondary behind starting outside cornerbacks Joey Porter and DaRon Bland.

Thomas will officially join the active roster with Dallas after being elevated from the practice squad for each of the team's last three contests. The 26-year-old will provide the team with an additional experienced option at safety moving forward.

Hufanga has missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury he suffered in Week 5 versus the Chargers. The safety appears likely to miss a third straight contest, and if that's the case, Devon Key would stand to draw another start in Denver's secondary Sunday versus the Chiefs.

Allen was a non-participant at practice to open the week Wednesday after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 7 versus Arizona, but he was able to return to the field Thursday. The defensive lineman will have one more chance to log a full practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Chiefs.

Mims was a limited participant in Wednesday's session, but the wideout's full participation a day later sets the stage for him to be available Sunday against the Chiefs. The 2023 second-rounder has two catches in each of his last three games, with his Week 8 fantasy upside linked to the status of top WR Jaylen Waddle, who is managing a chest injury.

Waddle departed in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's win at Arizona due to a chest injury, which limited him in practice last Wednesday and Thursday before he returned to a full session Friday and didn't enter the weekend with a designation. This week has been a different story, though, as he kicked it off with a DNP on Wednesday before Thursday's capped session. Friday's injury report will reveal Waddle's chances to suit up Sunday against the Chiefs.

Harvey wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so it's unclear if his limitations a day later stem from Denver's initial practice or were the result of an issue the running back encountered Thursday. In any case, added context with regard to Harvey's status for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will arrive no later than Friday. If available this weekend, Harvey will contend with J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman for Denver's Week 8 backfield touches.

Surtain practiced in a limited capacity last week before being inactive this past Sunday at Arizona, marking his third absence in a row due to a sprained ankle. With an uncapped session now under his belt, he's set for his first game action since Week 4, with the Broncos set to face the Chiefs this coming Sunday.
